Clay is the operator's spreadsheet — maximum control, you build the workflow. Different tools, often confused. Bottom line 11x and Clay get bundled into 'AI SDR' marketing but they're architecturally different categories. 11x is a full-stack platform that handles ICP discovery, enrichment, messaging, and sending — you provide an offer, it runs the outbound. Clay is an operator's workbench for designing your own enrichment-and-personalization pipeline; the platform doesn't send for you (you bring your own sender stack) and doesn't manage the SDR work itself. Teams using Clay successfully have a technical operator who builds the workflows; teams that buy Clay expecting an AI SDR are disappointed within weeks. Conversely, teams buying 11x expecting Clay-level control over enrichment and personalization find the platform's defaults more templated than they hoped. The right framing: 11x for teams that want to delegate outbound to a platform; Clay for teams that want to build a custom outbound stack with a technical operator at the wheel. 11x (Alice) vs. Clay feature and pricing comparison 11x (Alice) Clay Pricing Custom — typically thousands per month per AI rep. Starter $149/mo; Explorer $349/mo; higher tiers from $800/mo.
